program.name: Paralegal Studies Program, A.A.S.
program.minGrade: A grade of C or higher is required in all career studies courses. The catalog lists these classes under both LEGL and PLGL codes.

hero.title: Plan the route from your first class to your first paralegal job.
hero.sub: Pick the kind of legal work you want to do, then build the classes, certifications, and experience that get you there. Bring the finished plan to your advising appointment at Brookdale.
hero.goalDone: Your plan is ready for advising.
hero.goalTodo: Finish the steps to complete your plan.

steps.title: Choose 3 to 6 kinds of legal work
steps.intro: Paralegals work under a lawyer's supervision in many areas of law. Pick the ones that sound like work you'd enjoy. Your picks suggest which career studies classes to choose in step 2.

steps.title: Build your semester-by-semester plan
steps.intro: This is the catalog's suggested sequence. Seven of your classes are your choice from the career studies lists. Pick them here, check off what you've passed, and move a class to another term if you need to. The planner checks prerequisites and which terms each class runs.

steps.title: Decide about a professional certification
steps.intro: A certification is an exam-based credential from a national paralegal association. It is separate from your Brookdale degree.

steps.title: Pick the workplaces you'll target
steps.intro: Paralegals work in many kinds of organizations. Highlighted tags show where a workplace commonly hires for the careers you picked.

steps.title: Will you continue to a bachelor's degree?
steps.intro: This program is built for employment, not transfer, but it may transfer in part or in full to some four-year schools. If a bachelor's degree or law school is in your plans, say so now.

steps.title: Plan experience in a legal setting
steps.intro: Employers look for experience in a law office. The Paralegal Internship (LEGL 299) can count as one of your career studies choices.

steps.title: Review, save, and print
steps.intro: This is the plan you'll bring to advising. Save it to keep working later, print it, or download a copy.

entry: The suggested sequence assumes you have met all foundational studies requirements in reading, writing, and math.
Several career studies classes run only in Fall, only in Spring, or only in Summer. Choose yours early so the terms line up.

advice.text: In your first fall, a career studies choice that lists LEGL 105 as 'before or together with' (Real Property Transactions or Family Law) can be taken alongside LEGL 105. Classes that need LEGL 105 finished first have to wait.
The Paralegal Internship needs 30 credits, including all 16 credits of required career studies classes, so it belongs in your last term.

more.label: Occupational Outlook Handbook: paralegals and legal assistants

list.name: Litigation paralegal
list.desc: Prepares pleadings, organizes evidence and discovery, and helps attorneys get ready for trial in civil cases.

list.name: Personal injury paralegal
list.desc: Gathers medical records, drafts demand letters, and keeps injury cases moving.

list.name: Real estate paralegal
list.desc: Prepares contracts, title documents, and closing packages for property sales.

list.name: Title examiner or closing coordinator
list.desc: Searches property records and coordinates closings for a title company or lender.

list.name: Family law paralegal
list.desc: Drafts documents and works with clients in divorce, custody, support, and adoption matters.

list.name: Estates and probate paralegal
list.desc: Drafts wills and trusts and helps administer estates through probate.

list.name: Elder law paralegal
list.desc: Supports attorneys with guardianship, long-term care planning, and benefits for older clients.

list.name: Corporate paralegal
list.desc: Forms business entities, maintains corporate records, and prepares filings.

list.name: Contracts or compliance specialist
list.desc: Reviews and tracks contracts and helps an organization follow the rules that apply to it.

list.name: Criminal law paralegal
list.desc: Supports a prosecutor's or defense attorney's office with case files, motions, and court dates.

list.name: Court clerk or judiciary staff
list.desc: Processes filings and keeps the records and calendar of a court.

list.name: Government agency paralegal
list.desc: Researches regulations and prepares documents for a public agency.

list.name: Entertainment or intellectual property legal assistant
list.desc: Supports attorneys with contracts, licensing, and rights for artists and media companies.

list.name: Legal assistant in a general practice
list.desc: Handles a mix of client intake, drafting, and filing in a small firm that takes many kinds of cases.

certs.intro: Certification is voluntary. Check each organization's current eligibility rules before you plan an exam date, and ask your Legal Studies faculty which ones local employers value.

list.name: Certified Paralegal (CP)
list.desc: A widely recognized national exam covering legal knowledge and skills.

list.name: CORE Registered Paralegal (CRP)
list.desc: Earned by passing the Paralegal CORE Competency Exam, aimed at early-career paralegals.

list.name: Accredited Legal Professional (ALP)
list.desc: An entry credential covering office procedures, ethics, and legal knowledge.

list.name: New Jersey Notary Public commission
list.desc: A state commission, not a certification, that many law offices and title companies find useful.

list.name: Professional Paralegal (PP)
list.desc: An advanced exam for experienced paralegals.

list.name: PACE Registered Paralegal (RP)
list.desc: Earned by passing the Paralegal Advanced Competency Exam.

list.name: Advanced Certified Paralegal (ACP)
list.desc: Specialty credentials for paralegals who already hold the CP.

list.name: Small or solo law firm
list.note: A few attorneys handling many kinds of matters. You'll do a bit of everything.

list.name: Large law firm
list.note: Specialized practice groups and larger cases.

list.name: Corporate legal department
list.note: Working inside a company on its contracts, records, and compliance.

list.name: Government agency
list.note: Municipal, county, state, or federal offices, including prosecutors and public defenders.

list.name: Nonprofit and legal aid
list.note: Serving clients who can't afford a private attorney.
